title: United Nations Climate Change Conference

definition.text: The yearly conferences, known as COPs, at which the parties to the UN climate convention meet to assess and negotiate climate action.

facts.text: The first, COP 1, was held in Berlin in 1995.
Since 2005 they also serve as the meeting of the Kyoto Protocol's parties, and from 2011 to 2015 they were used to negotiate the Paris Agreement.
Any final text of a COP must be agreed by consensus.
Hosting rotates among the five UN regional groups.
More than 5,350 fossil fuel industry lobbyists attended the four conferences from 2021 to 2024.

prerequisites: United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change

title: Bali Action Plan
article: United Nations Climate Change Conference#2007: COP 13/CMP 3, Bali, Indonesia

definition.text: The 2007 decision at COP 13 in Bali that set a timeline and structure for negotiating a climate framework for after 2012.

facts.text: Developed countries agreed to comparable quantified emission targets, while developing countries agreed to nationally appropriate mitigation actions supported by technology, finance and capacity building.
It set up a new body, the Ad Hoc Working Group on Long-term Cooperative Action, for these negotiations, which ran through 2008 and 2009 toward Copenhagen.
The Bali conference also drew attention to the 20% of global emissions caused by deforestation.
